P1.3.text: RGC Resources is an energy services company engaged in the sale and distribution of natural gas to approximately 64,500 residential, commercial and industrial customers in Roanoke, Virginia, and the surrounding localities, through its Roanoke Gas subsidiary. In addition to Roanoke Gas, RGC Midstream is a subsidiary that invests in natural gas transportation infrastructure including the Mountain Valley Pipeline (MVP), MVP Southgate and MVP Boost.

P2.3.text: We grew up with the city.

P2.4.text: one year after Roanoke became a city, Roanoke Gas Company is proud to deliver safe, reliable, and affordable energy. Our mission is to improve the quality of life for the communities and customers we serve, and we joyfully honor that commitment every day.

P2.5.text: In those early years, gas replaced the oil and kerosene used to light the city’s streetlamps. As demand increased, we expanded to serve Salem and Vinton.

P2.6.text: Roanoke Gas Company transitioned from producing manufactured gas in local plants to tapping into natural gas pipelines throughout the region for distribution. Today, we serve more than 60,000 households, and the demand for clean, sustainable energy has never been higher.

P2.7.text: Our commitment extends beyond providing energy, though. In addition, all our officers serve on the boards of nonprofit organizations.

P2.8.text: One year after Roanoke was proclaimed a city, Roanoke Gas Company was founded by key leaders in an effort to develop the community. Founders included the first President, Peyton L. Terry, Secretary-Treasurer John H. Dunston, J.B. Austin, Alexander S. Asbury, Mortimer M. Rogers, John P. Pettyjohn, and William Welch.

P2.9.text: Roanoke City Extends Contract for 30 Years

P2.10.text: The Company’s franchise with the City of Roanoke, whose provisions included authorization for the City to purchase the gas property, was set to expire. The City chose to extend the franchise for another 30 years. With that, the leadership guided the Company through expansion and improvements.

P2.12.text: A new coal gas plant was constructed in order to provide the Gas Company with the most modern and efficient gas plant design available. The new holder was capable of storing 1,500,000 cubic feet and was at the time, one of the largest in Virginia

P2.13.text: Roanoke Gas Company Extends Service Area

P2.14.text: Gas mains are extended to Salem, Vinton, and other outlying suburbs at the time, including South Roanoke.

P2.15.text: The name of the gas company changed from Roanoke Gas Light Company to Roanoke Gas Company.

P2.16.text: Roanoke Gas Company Continues to Expand

P2.17.text: Growth continued as plans were developed to bring natural gas to Roanoke. Roanoke Gas received its certificate from the Federal Power Commission and organized the Roanoke Pipe Line Company to build a 30-mile pipeline from Gala, Virginia to Roanoke. It was completed in the late summer of 1950 and natural gas was introduced to homes and businesses. New natural gas rates were 20% lower than the manufactured gas rates and the BTU content was nearly double that of manufactured gas.
